summary:
We developed Dr. ORBIT, an autonomous, offline-first space health monitoring and telemetry platform tailored for astronauts on long-duration Artemis and Mars missions. During extended spaceflight, crew members face the five hazards of human spaceflight: space radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, altered gravity fields, and hostile closed environments leading to bone mineral density loss, muscle atrophy, cephalic fluid shifts, and circadian disruption. Communication delays of up to 22 minutes make real-time terrestrial medical guidance impossible.

Dr. ORBIT solves this by replacing static Earth-normal cutoffs with personalized statistical baseline learning and transparent Explainable AI ("Possible cause found from your data trends"). Astronauts can autonomously assess their cardiovascular and sleep indicators, scan NASA food pouches, track cumulative space radiation against NASA career limits, and record countermeasure workouts. Concurrently, flight physicians use a dedicated Doctor Console to triage crew urgency (High, Moderate, Stable), deliver clinical instructions with physiological "Why is that?" rationales, and manage emergency beacons. Operating 100% offline via browser IndexedDB, Dr. ORBIT guarantees clinical continuity where Earth cannot immediately answer.

details:
Dr. ORBIT is an autonomous, offline-first space health intelligence platform engineered for long-duration missions (Artemis Lunar Base & Mars transit) where light-speed latency isolates astronauts from real-time Earth medical support.

Rather than relying on generic population thresholds or opaque black-box AI, Dr. ORBIT computes mathematical personal baselines (μ, σ, rolling windows) derived exclusively from each astronaut's historical telemetry. It features Explainable AI that identifies physiological deviations (e.g., microgravity fluid redistribution, space osteopenia, circadian sleep debt) and articulates multi-indicator root causes using actual data trends. Astronauts log rations with an integrated NASA food pouch scanner, monitor cumulative space radiation against NASA limits, and perform countermeasure reviews.

Attending physicians utilize a dedicated Doctor Console to triage crew urgency (High, Moderate, Stable), review longitudinal biometrics, deliver clinical instructions with explicit 'Why is that?' physiological justifications, and manage emergency SOS beacons.

Built with React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, and IndexedDB (Dexie.js), the software operates 100% offline with zero cloud dependency. A unified global interface switcher lets operators instantly toggle between Laptop, Doctor, Mobile, and Telemetry views without friction, ensuring autonomous care and crew survival beyond Low Earth Orbit.
